data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Decentralized networks are more resilient to correlated failure specifically because they utilize a 'lazy consensus' or eventual consistency model, whereas large services often require strict consistency, which creates a positive feedback loop where a single component failure cascades into a global lock or outage.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the decentralized network uses a synchronous consensus algorithm (e.g., PBFT) that halts on failure.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the large service is designed to degrade gracefully to eventual consistency under partition.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Consistency Cascade: In a large service with strict consistency, a slow node can cause the entire system to halt, waiting for consensus. This turns an independent failure (one node crashing) into a correlated failure (all nodes timing out). Decentralized networks typically embrace eventual consistency, allowing the system to partition and continue operating, thus isolating the failure. The shared cause is the consistency protocol itself, which is triggered by the initial failure.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
